title: Properties of representable finite morphisms to Deligne--Mumford stacks
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal X$ be a Deligne--Mumford stack over $S$, let $\mathcal Y$ be a stack in groupoids over $S$, and let $v:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal X$ be representable finite. Here representable finite means that for each scheme $T\to\mathcal X$, the 2-fibre product $\mathcal Y\times_{\mathcal X}T$ is represented by a scheme finite over $T$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Then $\mathcal Y$ is a Deligne--Mumford stack over $S$, and $v$ is proper and locally quasi-finite as a morphism of stacks. Stack, Deligne--Mumford stack, algebraic space and 2-fibre product have the conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, def-trf-algebraic-space]. For morphisms of these stacks, locally of finite type is tested on smooth scheme charts using [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and finite type additionally requires quasi-compactness. Proper means finite type, universally closed, and having proper relative diagonal. Universally closed means that every base change induces a closed map of underlying point spaces. Locally quasi-finite means locally of finite type, with locally quasi-finite relative diagonal and discrete underlying point space of every field fibre. The point space of a stack consists of its field-valued objects up to isomorphism and common field extension, with the topology detected by a smooth scheme atlas. Properties of representable diagonals are tested on scheme charts; on schemes the proper and locally quasi-finite notions are [def-weil-proper-morphism, pqf-def-quasifinite].

proof.text: Fix an $S$-scheme $T$ and $y_1,y_2\in\mathcal Y(T)$. By [lem-sfb-dm-isom-space-unramified], $I=\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal X}(v y_1,v y_2)$ is an algebraic space over $T$; its unramifiedness is not needed. Put $P=\mathcal Y\times_{\mathcal X,v y_1}T$, a scheme by the representable finite hypothesis, and regard it as an algebraic space by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. There are two maps $a,b:I\to P$ over $T$: $a$ is given by $(y_1,\mathrm{id})$, and on a test scheme $Z\to I$ with universal isomorphism $\alpha:v y_1|_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}v y_2|_Z$, $b$ is given by $(y_2|_Z,\alpha^{-1})$. These formulas are natural under pullback and define the maps by the 2-fibre-product convention of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids].

source.place: Tag 045G (lemma-representable-diagonal), Isom-space test and explicit 2-fibre-product description

proof.text: Form $E=I\times_{(a,b),P\times_TP,\Delta_{P/T}}P$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] this is an algebraic space over $T$. For a scheme $Z\to T$, its $Z$-points are isomorphisms $\alpha:v y_1|_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}v y_2|_Z$ for which the two corresponding points of the scheme $P$ agree. By the arrow formula for the 2-fibre product in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], equality means exactly an arrow $\beta:y_1|_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}y_2|_Z$ with $v\beta=\alpha$. It is unique for this $\alpha$, because $P$ represents that fibred groupoid and thus has only identity automorphisms. Conversely every $\beta$ gives this equality. Hence $E$ represents $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal Y}(y_1,y_2)$, naturally in $Z$. A scheme test of $\Delta_{\mathcal Y/S}$ is precisely such an Isom functor, by the same 2-fibre-product definition. Thus $\Delta_{\mathcal Y/S}$ is representable by algebraic spaces.

source.place: Tag 045G (lemma-representable-diagonal); explicit equalizer in algebraic spaces, with spaces.tex Tag 02X2 (lemma-fibre-product-spaces)

proof.text: Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $p:U\to\mathcal X$, as supplied by the Deligne--Mumford hypothesis in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. The 2-fibre product $V=\mathcal Y\times_{\mathcal X}U$ is a scheme finite over $U$. For every scheme $T\to\mathcal Y$, the pullback $T\times_{\mathcal Y}V$ is canonically $T\times_{\mathcal X}U$: on objects the equivalence composes the two specified isomorphisms, with inverse inserting the given object of $\mathcal Y(T)$. Its projection to $T$ is representable etale and surjective by the scheme-test definition of the atlas $p$. Therefore $V\to\mathcal Y$ is a representable surjective etale scheme atlas. Together with step 2 and the assumed stack condition, this proves that $\mathcal Y$ is Deligne--Mumford. No flatness, etaleness or surjectivity of $v$ has been assumed.

source.place: Tag 05UM (lemma-representable-morphism-to-algebraic), pullback-atlas construction, specialized directly to an etale scheme atlas

proof.text: For an arbitrary scheme $T\to\mathcal X$, write $v_T:Y_T=\mathcal Y\times_{\mathcal X}T\to T$. The hypothesis says that this is a finite scheme morphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper] it is proper. By [pqf-lem-finite-qf] it is quasi-finite, hence locally quasi-finite: each point is isolated in its fibre and finite type supplies the local finite-type requirement in [pqf-def-quasifinite]. These assertions hold for every scheme test, including empty and nonreduced ones.

Both stacks are Deligne--Mumford by hypothesis and step 3, and $v$ is representable by schemes by the given scheme-test finiteness. Apply [lem-sfb-representable-stack-property-tests] to $f=v$. All its properness tests and all its local-quasi-finiteness tests hold by step 4. The two equivalences therefore give that $v$ is proper and locally quasi-finite as a stack morphism, with exactly the diagonal and point-space conditions of the statement.
